text: PR #5423 (#5420, atomic check-and-open primitive) merged as 880e1dc9f after 4 adversarial review rounds, each finding something real: round 1 (link_count wrongly included in the handle-based read's freshness check, caught by writing the regression test itself -- unlinking the checked path during the swap-scenario test legitimately drops st_nlink 1->0 with content untouched, spuriously failing); round 2 (no file-position reset meant a second call on the same handle read from stale EOF position -- fixed, then round 3's review found THAT fix introduced a real concurrent-access race: an ASan/UBSan harness empirically showed 1-5 of 8 concurrent reads on one handle corrupted via the shared lseek+read cursor -- fixed properly with position-independent pread()/OVERLAPPED-based ReadFile so concurrent calls never share mutable cursor state, verified via an 8-thread regression test); round 4 (the function returned the STALE check-time identity instead of the already-computed fresh post-read one, which several existing callers -- workspace_agent_target_containment.cpp, workspace_agent_process_containment.cpp, runtime_pipeline_package_content_io.cpp -- rely on as a hardlink-count security gate; fixed to return the fresh value, with a regression test adding a hard link mid-window). Also unified a duplicate struct pair and fixed a stale doc reference. One CI flake (unrelated Python-sidecar test) cleared by rerun after confirming via the parallel full-validation run it passed on the identical commit. Deferred cross-function read-loop duplication as issue #5424 rather than touching the pre-existing, already twice-reviewed string-reopening function's internals. Issue #5420 closed. Starting #5421 (migrate workspace_agent_process_parser.cpp's two check-then-read pairs to the new primitive) now, per explicit user pre-authorization to proceed straight through #5421/#5422 without checking in again.
